comment: Deliberate breakages of rules the release gates claim to enforce.
Each entry names the gate that must fail when the rule is removed.
`find` must appear exactly once in `file`; if it does not, the mutation
reports NOT_APPLIED rather than passing, because a manifest that has
drifted from the code tests nothing.

mutations.rule: A terminal receipt may not fill `finished_at` with the local clock when nothing reported a finish time.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the ledger records the time we looked, never a finish time we were not told

mutations.rule: Filesystem evidence must match the declared destination path, not just the digest.
mutations.find:
const matches = if (expected) |want|
                want.side == fx.side and
                    std.mem.eql(u8, want.path, fx.path) and
                    std.mem.eql(u8, want.sha256, fx.sha256)
            else
                false;
mutations.replace:
const matches = if (expected) |want|
                std.mem.eql(u8, want.sha256, fx.sha256)
            else
                false;
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a job's exit status cannot settle a transfer

mutations.rule: Filesystem evidence must have been read on the machine the transfer publishes to.
mutations.find:
const matches = if (expected) |want|
                want.side == fx.side and
                    std.mem.eql(u8, want.path, fx.path) and
                    std.mem.eql(u8, want.sha256, fx.sha256)
            else
                false;
mutations.replace:
const matches = if (expected) |want|
                std.mem.eql(u8, want.path, fx.path) and
                    std.mem.eql(u8, want.sha256, fx.sha256)
            else
                false;
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a job's exit status cannot settle a transfer

mutations.rule: A declared digest may never be overwritten.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the digest a transfer will be judged by is declared once, before it sends

mutations.rule: A digest may only be declared while the operation is still in created/connecting.
mutations.find:
\\   AND request_id IN (
        \\         SELECT request_id FROM operations
        \\          WHERE status IN ('created','connecting')
        \\       )
mutations.expect_gate: gate: the digest a transfer will be judged by is declared once, before it sends

mutations.rule: A checkpoint UPDATE that matches no row is an error, not a success.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a checkpoint write that lands on no row is an error, not a success

mutations.rule: A resume from a non-zero offset requires both the recorded and the observed prefix hash.
One request may hold at most one checkpoint, so it can declare at most one digest.
mutations.find: request_id        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES operations(request_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
mutations.replace: request_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES operations(request_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
mutations.expect_gate: gate: one request cannot hold two checkpoints, or two live transfers one destination

mutations.rule: At most one in-flight transfer may hold a given destination.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: one request cannot hold two checkpoints, or two live transfers one destination

mutations.rule: A non-zero confirmed offset requires a prefix hash to prove it.
mutations.find: \\  CHECK (confirmed_offset = 0 OR partial_sha256 IS NOT NULL),
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a confirmed offset without a prefix hash is refused by the schema

mutations.rule: Advancing the offset replaces the prefix hash; it may not keep the previous offset's proof.
mutations.expect_gate: gate: a confirmed offset without a prefix hash is refused by the schema

mutations.rule: A post-kill re-probe may only upgrade a cancellation when it establishes an exit code.
